I made a post of it in /introductions itself (https://voat.co/v/introductions/comments/104112)), but it was pointed out that this is probably a more suitable place for it.

I feel that /introductions is ultimately detrimental to the quality of the site as it functions at the moment. My concerns are as follows.

It's ostensibly the first page of the site for new users. That's where they'll go - as they are pushed to at the moment - to make their first interactions and form their first ideas and understanding of the site and its culture and preculiarities and distinctions. As it is set up, however, it functions as a positive-reinforcement-loop and a 'safe place' hugbox - anyone who goes there will have their post positively recieved regardless of quality and intention. They will see their behavior vindicated in their own eyes and take it to other subforums with them instead of going to the subforums firstly and acclimatising to their new environs.

Removing /introductions and guiding new users towards more specific yet still general and perhaps somewhat more regulated subforums corresponding to their intrests wouldn't result in a loss of anything valuable - people can still get and offer help, guidance and waypoints towards more specific and less regulated forums without the constant circlejerking, blogging and hugbox nice-guy-points farming.

Also, this is another thing - why is accuring points just for the sake of it even encouraged at all? Points should be something that are the by-product of quality posts not ever a goal in itself. Why should effortlessly accuring points in /introductions for nothing more than posting dank memes or blogging about oneself or literally just saying 'I'll stick around if this gets big and my reddit-points become worthless' afford ones opinion higher value in a discussion about, say bikes in /dirtbikes than the regular users?

Why don't you just block it (as I already suggested) and move on? I don't think we want to set a precedent by removing (to you) an unpopular subverse.

If we start there, where does it end?
We can't just remove subverted because you don't like the content, I believe that is what many users are escaping from. As long as their are new users it provides a sub where they start out.

Blocking would just be ignoring the symtom not addressing the problem. Sure, that's probably what I'll end up doing after I've had my say and discussion had died down fruitlessly. But that's not a solution.

The problem is, that /introductions isn't set up to be just any subforum. It's one that new users are pointed towards and one that produces nothing of value at all. This encourages new users to take the same attitude elsewhere. Those posts would be fine they were contained to a subforum with reddit in the title or where ever else they'd be most relevant, but not on an orientation forum.

Though, there would still be the problem of points. By accuring points in /introductions or /redditisdone4 for nothing worthwhile at all, those points can then be taken to another subforum and their weight thrown around. This seems undeserved and unfair not to mention detrimental for the site itself.

Also, the possibility of accuring points will foster certain behaviors with point-farming and throwing their weight around being among them.

I'll restate my proposal concisely:

-remove /introductions and point new users towards general subforums - that is gaming, science, music etc.

-consider reworking points - making them affect only each relevant subforum - or remove them entirely while keeping the boats.

So what happens the next time someone doesn't like a subverse? We remove that one as well? Then the next? And the next?

No thank you.

This is not about me subjectively liking or not liking a random subforum. This is me thinking that /introductions as a place for orientation for new users isn't beneficial for the site in its current iteration. It could easily be removed and its role divided among other general subforums for overall better quality. I think that my fears are grounded, my reasoning sound and my solution solid so I've brought this to the spotlight to be debated over.

You don't think the information provided in the sidebar is pertinent and important for new users to know? How is providing a single place new users can get oriented and acquainted a bad thing? Some people choose to be social. Nobody forces them to come participate in the subverse. They are just as free to block it as you are.

People have a choice, you seem to want to remove that freedom of choice. I would hazard to say that's a big red flag. Voat is about freedom, not censorship. You go do your thing and allow everyone else to do theirs.

I disagree with the notion that there is anything wrong with having a bit of a love-bomb area like /v/introductions. Just because reddit has a lot of jaded curmudgeons doesn't mean voat needs to as well. :P

As you said, it's an important part of establishing the culture of the community here. Would you prefer people not feel welcomed and respected? The thing that makes voat great for me is that culture of mutual respect and courtesy that seems to dominate. It's wonderful. How is this anything like a "safe space"? Just because it's friendly here doesn't mean there is an illness.

Hey, i am not sure if this belongs here and excuse my English.

I am training everyday for the past 3 months but since i was and am a very skinny guy i want some more definition on my muscles.

I was 59kg with a height of 181cm. I am now at 70kg but can't gain any more no matter how much i eat. and i eat a fucking lot.

Now my training teacher told me to buy Nuetrent whey 100% protein and gave a schedule to drink that with water 3 times a day.

Can someone explain this alittle bit more to me and tell me if it will benefit the cause?

You gained 11kg in 3 months. If you were training hard, maybe 6/8 kg of this is muscle, thanks to so called "newbie gains". But this is probably over, now the gains will be much slower.

What you need to do is:

1) Establish your baseline caloric requirements, add around 500, while keeping your marcros(carbs, proteins, fats) in check (you can use http://iifym.com/tdee-calculator/)

2) Train hard (and consider having off days, everyday is too much for most people)

3) Adjust 1) if needed.

4) Repeat

Progress is measured in months or even years, you cannot expect to grow kilograms every month, unless you want to be fat.

Thank god the developers didn't implement fall damage.
